Update a govReactable caption or subtitle from the server

Source: R/update_reactable_caption.R
update_reactable_caption.Rd

Changes the caption, the subtitle, or both, of a govReactableOutput() table while the app is running, for example so the title still describes the data after a filter changes it.

The caption and subtitle are the table's accessible name, so keeping them accurate matters for screen reader users as well as sighted users.

The new text isn't announced when it changes, because it follows something the user just did, such as picking a filter. Screen readers read the new title when the user reaches the table.

Works inside Shiny modules without extra namespacing: pass the same output_table_name you used in renderGovReactable().

Usage

update_reactable_caption(
  session,
  output_table_name,
  caption = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

Arguments

session

The Shiny session object

output_table_name

The id of the table, as given to govReactableOutput() and output$<id> (without the module namespace)

caption

The new caption, or NULL (default) to leave it as it is. Plain text is escaped and shown as written; use shiny::HTML() or tags for markup

subtitle

The new subtitle, or NULL (default) to leave it as it is. Escaped in the same way as caption. Only works if govReactableOutput() was given a subtitle to start with

Value

NULL (invisibly), called for side effects

See also

Other Govstyle tables tabs and accordions: accordion(), govReactable(), govReactable-shiny, govTable(), govTabs()

Examples

colours <- sort(unique(shinyGovstyle::transport_data$colours))

ui <- shinyGovstyle::gov_page(
  shinyGovstyle::select_Input(
    inputId = "colour",
    label = "Colour",
    select_text = colours,
    select_value = colours
  ),
  shinyGovstyle::govReactableOutput(
    "table",
    # Start with the title for the dropdown's default choice
    caption = paste(colours[1], "vehicle costs peaked in March"),
    subtitle = paste(colours[1], "vehicle costs (£), January to May")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$table <- shinyGovstyle::renderGovReactable({
    shinyGovstyle::govReactable(
      subset(shinyGovstyle::transport_data, colours == input$colour)
    )
  })

  shiny::observe({
    shinyGovstyle::update_reactable_caption(
      session,
      "table",
      caption = paste(input$colour, "vehicle costs peaked in March"),
      subtitle = paste(input$colour, "vehicle costs (£), January to May")
    )
  })
}

if (interactive()) shiny::shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
